text:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a dedicated "hotpath-proxy" service that handles latency-critical inference requests (short-circuit routing, KV cache lookup, batching hints). Aim: isolate hotpath complexity from control plane and make independent scaling/rollouts possible. Thoughts?
maria: curious on scope. is this just a routing/fast-path proxy or are we moving cache ownership + affinity?
alex: initial proposal: proxy = stateless router + local fast KV cache read through a thin memstore client. Ownership of authoritative KV remains in cache-service for writes; proxy keeps a short-lived LRU for reads. No authoritative state in proxy.
ben: worried about consistency — if proxy reads stale cache it could affect outputs for a small % of requests. do we have examples where that matters?
jamie: for short-lived prefix caching it's usually fine; we already accept eventual consistency for some reranking counters. need clear correctness invariants though.
sahil: performance gains estimate? any numbers?
alex: eyeballing: reduce p50 by ~10-20ms on our hotpath for small prompts because we avoid an extra RPC hop and can do micro-batching. p95 improvement depends on queueing; should reduce tail by avoiding control-plane contention.
lisa: operational complexity: more services to deploy, instrument, secure. How do we prevent fallback chaos if proxy is misbehaving?
maria: think we need automatic fallback to control-plane router + a rate limiter in proxy. + circuit breaker metrics exposed.
ben: also need a migration strategy: start as opt-in per-route, then flip flag at tenant-level. doable?
alex: agree. migration plan sketch: 1) build proxy behind feature flag (off) 2) route canaries from dev/test tenants 3) enable for low-risk prod routes 4) monitor metrics + ramp.
jamie: metrics to watch: end-to-end latency, error-rate, cache hit ratio, duplicate-request rate, model token per-second. Add synthetic traces for strictness.
sahil: load testing plan: run soak with realistic KV hit/miss ratio and simulate control-plane outage to validate fallback. Also test cold-start behavior.
infrastructure note — infra-bot: new service will need autoscaling policies (min 2, scale by p95 CPU and p99 latency), egress limits, and IAM role for memstore reads.
lisa: add alerting runbook: if proxy error-rate > 0.5% for 5m -> auto-disable feature flag for that route and page oncall.
ben: what about security boundary? proxy will see tokens. will it validate auth itself or pass-through?
alex: proxy should validate bearer token and forward a short-lived attestation to control-plane for audit. No token caching. Keep logs redacted.
maria: deployment packaging: container + small native binary (go) with ischemic startup. share a sample config?
alex: snippet: ```yaml
hotpath_proxy:
  listen: 0.0.0.0:8080
  memstore: memstore://cache-service:11211
  fallback_router: https://router.internal
  feature_flag: ff.hotpath_proxy
  batch_window_ms: 5
```
jamie: batch_window_ms = 5 seems reasonable to avoid latency cliffs. allow per-route override.
sahil: quantization/compat: some model kernels expect special headers for KV shapes — proxy must be model-agnostic. suggest a pluginable adapter interface but keep initial impl generic.
lisa: remind: add privacy review — proxy touching prompts is sensitive. redact before logging and add KMS integration for attestation.
alex: agreed. open items: detailed SLA for proxy, cost model, rollback criteria. I'll draft RFC update with canary checklist and perf targets.
ben: +1. include a small AB test design to ensure output quality isn't impacted.
maria: I'll volunteer to own the canary and metrics dashboard.
jamie: I'll help write integration tests and load harness.
sahil: I'll validate autoscaling and failure modes.
infra-bot: deploy-bot will create a staging job template when RFC lands in proposals repo.
alex: thanks all — I'll post RFC update by EOD with next steps and link to the proposals PR.
